title: Masked source boundaries
responsibility: Tracks bracket depths and finds approximate statement and function-body bounds in masked source.

inputs.name: statementEnd.masked
inputs.description: Masked source text that statementEnd scans forward from statementEnd.start, testing characters at start's brace and group depth for `;`, a newline or `}`; the newline test reads up to 40 characters after that newline, and an empty string makes the result -1.

inputs.name: statementEnd.nesting
inputs.description: Depth arrays from sourceNesting for the same masked source; statementEnd reads both its brace and group arrays and considers only offsets whose depths equal those at statementEnd.start.

inputs.name: statementEnd.start
inputs.description: Offset into the masked source where the scan begins, inclusive; its brace and group depths set the level that later characters must match, and a newline at this offset never ends the statement.

inputs.name: sourceNesting.masked
inputs.description: Masked source text, expected to have literal and comment contents already masked out, whose `{`, `}`, `(`, `)`, `[` and `]` characters are each counted as they appear; sourceNesting does not parse strings or comments itself.

inputs.name: matchingBrace.nesting
inputs.description: Depth arrays from sourceNesting for the same masked source; matchingBrace reads only the brace array, and that array's length sets the fallback result when no closing brace is found.

inputs.name: matchingBrace.open
inputs.description: Offset of the opening `{` whose closing brace is wanted; matchingBrace takes the brace depth at this offset as its target and searches from open + 1, without checking that the character there is `{`.

inputs.name: bodyEnd.masked
inputs.description: Masked source text that bodyEnd scans from bodyEnd.from for a `;` or a `{` at from's group depth; after each such `{` it reads up to 39 characters past the matching `}` to decide whether to skip that block as a return type.

inputs.name: bodyEnd.nesting
inputs.description: Depth arrays from sourceNesting for the same masked source; bodyEnd reads the group array for its level checks and passes the whole object to matchingBrace, which reads the brace array.

inputs.name: bodyEnd.from
inputs.description: Offset where the body search starts; the scan includes this offset, and its group depth sets the parenthesis and square-bracket level that a body `{` or `;` must share.

outputs.name: sourceNesting
outputs.description: Two Int32Arrays of length masked.length + 1: `brace` holds the curly-brace depth before each character and `group` holds a shared count of `(` and `[` minus `)` and `]` before each character, with the last entry giving the depth after the final character. Depths are not clamped, so unmatched closing characters can make them negative.

outputs.name: matchingBrace
outputs.description: Offset of the `}` at which the brace depth first returns to the value it had at `open`; when that never happens the result is nesting.brace.length - 2, which is the last source offset for arrays from sourceNesting.

outputs.name: statementEnd
outputs.description: Scanning forward at start's brace and group depth, the inclusive end is a `;` itself, or the character before a `}` or before a newline after start that begins a recognized statement, and masked.length - 1 when none of these occurs. A newline begins a recognized statement when the next non-blank text within 40 characters starts with one of the whole words export, const, let, var, function, class, import, interface, type, if, for, return, async, declare or enum, or with `}` or `)`, or when only blank text remains within those 40 characters.

outputs.name: bodyEnd
outputs.description: Inclusive offset of the `}` closing the first `{` at from's group depth that is not skipped as a return type, or -1 when a `;` at that depth is reached first or no such brace exists. A `{` block whose closing brace is followed, after only spaces or tabs, by `{`, `|`, `&`, `[`, `>`, `,`, `)` or `=>` is skipped as a return type, and an unclosed body yields masked.length - 1.
